text: Oakmere Credit Union's regulatory exam flagged weak MFA coverage. Renata Ibarra's fix starts here: one Conditional Access policy, CA-RequireMFA-AllUsers, requiring multi-factor authentication for every sign-in into the oakmere-cu tenant.

But three legacy service accounts can't do interactive MFA yet -- so the plan names them. CA-Legacy-ServiceAccounts-Exempt holds exactly three accounts, written down as a temporary, risk-accepted exception, not a quiet gap.
Oakmere's AWS access gets consolidated too, through AWS IAM Identity Center federated to Entra ID -- one identity, one MFA posture, one audit trail across both clouds.
The plan doesn't stop at the exception. Quarterly access reviews, a migration path to certificate-based authentication, and a committed date to retire the exclusion group entirely.
Next: what happens if one of those three exempted accounts is ever compromised -- planning the network segmentation that contains it.
